### Orchestrate

**You own the unit graph, every launch, and accepted integration.** Workers execute bounded units, never sub-coordinate or publish.

Read the [sign-off contract](../references/sign-off.md) before preparation or implementation and [run accounting](../references/run-contract.md) before dispatch.

1. Resolve the plan and actual attributable approval/grant. If the plan is missing or incomplete, use [Multi-phase plan](multi-phase-plan.md) for preparation and one proposal, not speculative dispatch. Existing approval can cover the exact units without another checkpoint. Record exclusions, stop conditions, action/budget bounds, plan/source references, and the falsifiable whole-run done predicate.
2. Initialize or recover the run store outside product and cleanup targets. Validate stable units/dependencies. Name exclusive outputs and integration ownership. Unknown workers retain reservations. Explicitly reconcile native handles and workspaces; PID existence or a summary is not proof of identity/completion. Reserve before launching, so a crash between launch and handle recording cannot silently duplicate work.
3. Pilot one unit end to end before widening. Its brief carries attributable authority context or evidence, actual dependency inputs, target workspace/head, file scope, acceptance commands, exclusions, stop conditions, budget, and report/output location. Use existing configured `implementer`, `implementer-hard`, or `judgment` roles per the coordinator's Subagents section. The root owns every spawn.
4. Inspect the worker's actual result, integrate serially, and verify the integrated artifact. Bind the receipt to repository/workspace identity, head, dirty-content digest, attempt, dependency receipts, and real evidence. When integration advances the snapshot, re-run relevant upstream verification in dependency order for the same completed attempts. Append `record_receipt` with `reverifies` naming each latest passing receipt and fresh `acceptance_receipts` naming its re-verified dependencies. Accept the new unit with its original immutable `input_receipts` and those fresh acceptance IDs. Never substitute another work attempt or an old test log as new proof. A failed attempt can record failure evidence without claiming successful upstream acceptance. Finished is not verified. Type-only, inconclusive, failed, or stale receipts cannot release dependencies. Preserve history instead of clearing old proof.
5. Widen to at most two in-flight workers unless the user set another bound. Launch ready units only after valid dependency outputs/receipts are relayed and present in their workspace. Disjoint outputs permit parallelism; coupled code or one shared branch serializes. Use **swarm** for a coverage/race step and **candidate-graft** only for an approved comparison needing synthesis, not to delegate running this playbook.
6. Reconcile each worker as reserved/running/unknown/finished/failed/blocked/abandoned. Process exit does not discard finished unverified work. An intentional retirement uses evidence-backed `abandon_attempt`, preserving its finish and output history rather than marking it stopped. After an interruption, inspect native state and evidence before retries. Unknown writers keep their output; retry only in a fresh isolated output or after confirmed abandonment. Changes to a dependency, plan, or scope invalidate affected acceptance and return a revised proposal when authority does not cover them. Keep unaffected covered work moving.
7. Refresh required receipts at the final snapshot in dependency order, then run the whole predicate and **review-panel**, not just unit self-reports. Use [Opening a PR](opening-a-pr.md) only within delivery bounds. No landing/merge frontier, nested cloud fleet, or scheduler. At a budget/stop/blocker, use [Pause safely](pause-safely.md) and account for all remaining units.

**Reply:** run/plan/store paths, accepted integrated units and exact proof, running/unknown/blocked units, actual delivery, budgets/stop reason, and pickup action. A partial graph is not completion.
